payload.title: Garden Wedding Ideas and What to Plan For
payload.meta_title: Garden Wedding Ideas and What to Plan For
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with AUD 150k or more to spend who love the look of a garden wedding, here or abroad, and want two things from one page: real garden weddings they can look at, and a plain list of what a garden actually asks of the day (rain, heat, sun, uneven ground, older guests, insects, curfews, power and the garden's own rules) so they know what to ask a venue before they fall for it.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor (one click to the Wedded Concierge page), with the magazine as the early stage lead magnet secondary.
payload.angle: Page one for garden wedding is mostly mood boards and venue directories. This page starts from garden weddings we have actually published, introduced by the couples' names as each story names them, then turns the look into decisions: styling ideas for aisles, long tables, greenery, dusk lighting, lounges and stationery, and a set of questions to put to any garden venue about the things that go wrong outdoors (a wet weather plan and covered space, heat, shade and sun, ground and footwear, access for older guests with a route without steps, insects, noise and curfew, power and lighting, and garden protection rules). It is honest that a garden is beautiful and also the venue most exposed to weather, and it gives couples planning abroad the questions to ask, not promises.

sections.heading: none (intro)
sections.brief: Direct answer in 2 to 3 sentences: a garden wedding is a ceremony, reception or both held outdoors among planted grounds, lawns or orchards, and it works when the styling and the backup plan are decided together. Then exactly 4 takeaways, each one sentence: (1) the real garden weddings below come from our own published stories; (2) the styling ideas cover the aisle, tables, greenery, lighting, lounges and stationery; (3) the planning points are questions to ask the venue, starting with the wet weather plan and covered space; (4) planning a garden wedding abroad adds questions about season, travel and who looks after the day, which a Wedded Advisor can answer for your dates.

sections.heading: Real garden weddings from our pages
sections.brief: One short card per wedding from the SEO step's real wedding map (02-seo.json). Each card: the couple's names exactly as the published story names them, the setting described without the venue name (for example 'a garden estate', 'a villa terrace', 'a walled garden'), one or two details the story itself states, and one link to the story. Nothing added beyond what each story says; no vendor or venue names even if the story names them; no dates, guest counts or locations unless the story states them. Expected to include /tommy-winkler-jessica-pappas-european-garden-inspired-wedding and /trending/valerie-lungus-civil-wedding-had-the-dreamiest-garden-party-setting if the SEO step confirms both are live and describe a garden setting. If fewer than 2 stories qualify, keep the section with what exists and say so in the run report.

sections.heading: Garden wedding ideas
sections.brief: Styling ideas only, as short subsections: ceremony aisles and arches; long tables; florals and greenery as design choices; lighting for dusk; lawn games and lounges; stationery. No seasonal flower claims (what is in season when) unless sourced; point to the flowers in season hub instead. Link /style-advice/wedding-table-decor and /style-advice/22-amazing-table-settings-for-every-wedding-theme where they fit, /style-advice/wedding-centrepieces only if live (else <!-- LINK: /style-advice/wedding-centrepieces when live -->), and the flowers hub /style-advice/fashionable-flowers-opt-for-in-season-or-order-imported. Optionally /expert-advice/wedding-without-seating-chart for lounge or open seating (live as at 2026-11-20).

sections.heading: What to plan for in a garden
sections.brief: Each point is written as questions to ask the venue, with one or two lines of why: a wet weather plan and covered space (where it is, how many it holds, when the call is made); heat, shade and sun (shade for the ceremony, water, timing; any sun safety line only from Cancer Council or ARPANSA via batch gw_a, linked at the claim); ground and footwear (lawn, gravel, slopes, heels); access for older guests and a route without steps (from arrival to ceremony, tables and bathrooms); insects (what the venue does and when); noise and curfew (amplified music limits and finish times, asked not stated); power and lighting (what power exists outdoors, generators, path lighting after dark); garden protection rules (confetti, candles, staking, marquee pegs, areas guests cannot enter). Never state a venue's rule, capacity or curfew as fact.

sections.heading: Destination garden weddings
sections.brief: Questions only for couples marrying abroad in a garden: which months suit the garden at that destination, what the covered backup is, how guests travel between hotel and garden, who is on the venue's side on the day, and what the garden allows for set up and pack down. No destination weather or season claims. Links to /destination-weddings/wedding-destinations-november, /destinations/oceania and month pages only if live, otherwise LINK comments. The single body Wedded Advisor line sits here with the Concierge secondary CTA (anchor 'Wedded Concierge'). Magazine magnet link here or after the ideas section (/magazine with UTM).

sections.heading: Garden wedding FAQ
sections.brief: 4 to 6 questions (questions allowed here only), for example: What is a garden wedding? What should a garden wedding have as a wet weather plan? What do guests wear to a garden wedding? How do you light a garden wedding at night? Can you have a garden wedding abroad? Answers repeat body content only, no new claims.
